fields.value: Rent GPU machines from AWS EC2

## Problem

Etude rents machines from RunPod, Vast and Lium only. On 2026-11-17 all three had no rentable GPU for most of a morning (L4, 4090, 3090, A5000, A6000 checked repeatedly), one Vast host died, another stalled on disk writes, and Lium rental is broken (Task 73e1a9). A measurement approved at USD 3 took four rentals and still had no number. There is no source with dependable on-demand capacity and ordinary durable disks.

AWS appears in Etude only as S3 storage.

## Outcome

AWS EC2 is a fourth provider, behind the same on-demand templates, `etude availability`, `etude rent`, cost cap, machine timer and launcher cleanup as the others.

- On-demand GPU instances first (g6 / L4 as the reference). Spot is a later step; a reclaimed spot instance is the interruption the save-and-resume work already handles.
- A rented instance is always terminated: the stranded-machine failure in 73e1a9 must not be possible here (find by tag, terminate by tag).
- Price comes from AWS, not a table in the code.
- Proven end to end once: rent, run something, terminate, confirmed absent.

## Constraints

- Credentials come from the environment or Doppler, as for the other providers; none in the repository.
- The account's GPU quota ("Running On-Demand G and VT instances") starts at zero vCPUs on a new account; `etude availability` should say when quota, not capacity, is the refusal.
- No dependency for people who do not use AWS beyond the existing optional boto3.
